newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany will fulfil EMU criteria in 1997-minister.
newsitem.headline: Germany will fulfil EMU criteria in 1997-minister.

text.p: Germany and France will meet the necessary criteria for European Monetary Union in 1997, German Chancellery Minister Friedrich Bohl said in an interview with the newspaper Welt am Sonntag, to be published on Sunday.

Bohl said that the introduction of Germany's different austerity measures would bring federal, regional and local deficits, as well as social insurance deficits, under the three percent set out in the Maastricht criteria.
France would also meet the criteria, "despite the fears of some people," Bohl said.
The French government had proposed an ambitious, but realistic, budget plan which foresaw a budget deficit below three percent of GDP, the level required to meet EMU conditions, Bohl said.
He added that similar savings plans in other European countries gave hope that "as many countries as possible" would fulfil the requirements.
Figures for 1997 would decide which countries would take part in part in currency union in 1999, Bohl said.
